drug_class: Targeted cancer therapy (EGFR inhibitor / tyrosine kinase inhibitor)
purpose: Gefitinib is used to treat a certain type of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It is specifically used when the cancer has a particular gene change (mutation) in a protein called EGFR. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medication is the right fit for you.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have an abnormal protein called EGFR that tells them to grow and multiply out of control. Gefitinib works like a targeted 'off switch' — it blocks this protein so the cancer cells can no longer get the signal to grow. Because it targets a specific change in cancer cells, it tends to spare many normal healthy cells compared to traditional chemotherapy.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dry or itchy skin, acne-like rash on the face and body, mouth sores, and changes in your nails. Some people also notice dry eyes or blurred vision.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you develop sudden or worsening shortness of breath, cough, or fever — these could be signs of a serious lung problem called interstitial lung disease. Gefitinib can also cause liver problems, so your doctor will check your blood regularly. It can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control during treatment. Avoid grapefruit and certain other medications that can interfere with how this drug works in your body.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 250 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose, in which case just skip the missed one. Never take two doses at the same time.
